Entries.SourceTerm: 始從芳草去，又逐落花回

Senses.PreferredTarget: I went out among fragrant grasses and returned following falling blossoms.
SearchAliases: I went out among fragrant grasses and returned following falling blossoms
Senses.Note: The image makes a Chan return from wandering into a direct report of spring, then becomes a test of what was actually seen. The spring scene is not itself proof of realization.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃云：「僧問趙州：『萬法歸一。』且道與第一義底一是同是別？州云：『我在青州作領布衫重七斤。』且道與第一義已前消息是同是別？若道同，朗州山、澧州水，四海五湖王化裡；若道別，豆子山打瓦鼓，陽平山下白雨。也不同、也不別，滕王高閣臨江渚，佩玉鳴鑾罷歌舞。今日尹參府皈依佛法，也只為這第一義；受持五戒，也只為這第一義；因戒生定，因定發慧，因慧參得自性念佛底主人公，也只為這第一義。且道如何是第一義？咦！」上堂。「冬至日，一線天，地雷復，柳含煙，遍地紅輪，真箇是葉上霜珠圓更圓。佛身充滿於法界，普現一切群生前，鷲峰峰下重相見，鼻孔原來總一般。急吐卻，野狐涎，驊騮馬，珊瑚鞭，一騎紅塵妃子笑，等閑不許外人看。為甚麼不許外人看？路逢劍客須呈劍，不是詩人莫獻詩。」問：「如何是佛？」師云：「拄杖撐著月。」「如何是祖？」師云：「橫肩兩樣看。」「如何是超佛越祖？」師云：「提起三十棒。」僧一喝，師拍掌三下。病中，上堂。「維摩病在毘耶城，老僧病在聚雲寺，兩箇無孔鐵鎚，一前一後相似。今日若有人問話，但只搖手。如云：『不會。』向道：『老僧感冒傷風，失了聲氣。』」元旦上堂。舉：「長沙岑遊山歸，首座問：『遊山事作麼生？』岑云：『始從芳草去，又逐落花回。』座云：『大似春意。』岑云：『也勝秋露滴芙蓉。』若有人問聚雲：『遊山事作麼生？』但道：『倒騎鐵馬飛金雨，呀吒獅子吼雲騰。』若問：『長沙和尚語中帶有春意，因甚和尚全無？』但道：『去年正月也有今日，前年正月也有今日，明年正月也有今日，後年正月也有今日，晝夜十二時，九十六成經，三百六十日，二十四成綸，和氣暖風調宇宙，大地何方不是春？』」崇禎丁丑二月望日，尹參府遂江居士請師於巴臺禪院結制。山門。「十方薄伽梵，一路涅槃門。既是一路涅槃門，也不須門外打之遶。」佛殿。「金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，如何即得？」立定，云：「佛陀耶。」展具，云：「達磨耶。」合十，云：「僧伽耶。」禮拜起，復云：「聻。」方丈。「古人喚作方丈地，老僧喚作方丈室。將來烹佛煉祖，道是衲僧巴鼻。」喝一喝。上堂。拈香罷，維那白槌，師隨喝一喝，云：「玄要料揀，賓主照用，一並漏逗了也。若也不會，聽取一偈：野寺孤明夜月斜，高臺飛閣遠人家，綠水金輝浮桂影，青山玉曉墮霜華。」問：「心佛與眾生是三無差別，如何是心？」師云：「門前幾竿竹。」進云：「如何是佛？」師云：「嶺上數株松。」進云：「還有眾生也無？」師云：「心佛與眾生是三無差別。」僧

Occurrences.Kwic: 一片，更於何處覓封疆。趙州勘婆子。頌：蕩蕩一條官驛路，行人往往問前津，自從勘破歸來也，誰觸長安車馬塵。趙州因秀才問：「佛不違眾生願，是否？」州云：「是。」曰：「某甲欲覓和尚手中拄杖，得否？」州云：「君子不奪人所好。」曰：「某甲非君子。」曰：「我亦不是佛。」頌：當機一拶玄關轉，走馬循環不暫停，趙老雖然能作主，看來也是假惺惺。趙州無字。頌：一朝被蛇傷，怕見斷井索，總然道個無，爭免狂風作。鎮州蘿蔔。頌：鎮州出大蘿蔔，拈來百味俱足，須知不著薑椒，趙老家風別俗。巖頭作渡次，一日因婆子抱個兒來，乃曰：「呈橈舞棹即不問，且道婆子手中兒甚處得來？」頭便打。婆曰：「婆生七子，六個不遇知音，祇這一個也不消得。」便拋向水中。頌：獨泛悠悠一小舟，滄溟突出巨鰲頭，攔腮一掣翻身去，今古長江水自流。張拙秀才看《千佛名經》，問長沙曰：「百千諸佛，但見其名，未審居何國土，還化物也無？」沙曰：「黃鶴樓崔顥題後，秀才還曾題也未？」曰：「未曾。」沙曰：「得閒題取一篇。」頌：百千諸佛居何土，月印長江徹底清，黃鶴樓題崔顥後。至今吟韻許誰賡？長沙一日游山歸，首座曰：「問和尚甚處去來？」沙曰：「游山來。」座曰：「到甚麼處？」沙云：「始從芳草去，又逐落花回。」座曰：「大似春意。」沙曰：「也勝秋露滴芙蓉。」頌：落花舖徑亂啼鶯，無事野人策杖行，踏遍芳叢歸去也，報君春色勝秋榮。巖頭在鄂渚湖，三文錢買個黑撈波，每日撈蝦捕蜆，且恁麼過時。頌：鄂渚州頭生意足，扁舟獨泛出塵俗，乘風一笛過滄溟，煙樹依依江畔宿。南院問僧：「名甚麼？」曰：「普參。」院曰：「忽遇屎橛時如何？」曰：「不審。」院便打。頌：古佛家風輕漏洩，銀蟾出海對君說。對君說，太饒舌，笑殺雲門屎一橛。溈山問仰山：「如何是西來大意？」仰云：「大好燈籠。」頌：大好燈籠，逼塞虛空，西來大意，門對爐峰。僧問龍牙和尚：「蘇嚕蘇嚕，還有西來意也無？」牙云：「蘇嚕蘿嚕。」頌：腳踏毘盧頂上行，從來不識野狐禪，江山風月由君弄，已落胡笳別調弦。風吹別調露真機，直下全提半似痴，其中消息誰能會，試聽春山啼子規。無位真人。頌：酒色之徒，橫眠倒拖。無位真人攔不住，得歡樂處且歡歌。逢人舉手話淆訛，無位真人好大歌，今日分明通一線，大家依樣畫葫蘆。世尊睹明星悟道。頌：明星忽睹豁雙眼，遍界風光不可藏，鼻直眉橫成現事，笑他特地語郎當。忽睹明星也大奇，驚天動地小兒戲，娘生鼻孔突然現，額下橫分兩道眉。黃龍三關。頌：我手何似佛手，喜怒誰

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 乃云：「僧問趙州：『萬法歸一。』且道與第一義底一是同是別？州云：『我在青州作領布衫重七斤。』且道與第一義已前消息是同是別？若道同，朗州山、澧州水，四海五湖王化裡；若道別，豆子山打瓦鼓，陽平山下白雨。也不同、也不別，滕王高閣臨江渚，佩玉鳴鑾罷歌舞。今日尹參府皈依佛法，也只為這第一義；受持五戒，也只為這第一義；因戒生定，因定發慧，因慧參得自性念佛底主人公，也只為這第一義。且道如何是第一義？咦！」上堂。「冬至日，一線天，地雷復，柳含煙，遍地紅輪，真箇是葉上霜珠圓更圓。佛身充滿於法界，普現一切群生前，鷲峰峰下重相見，鼻孔原來總一般。急吐卻，野狐涎，驊騮馬，珊瑚鞭，一騎紅塵妃子笑，等閑不許外人看。為甚麼不許外人看？路逢劍客須呈劍，不是詩人莫獻詩。」問：「如何是佛？」師云：「拄杖撐著月。」「如何是祖？」師云：「橫肩兩樣看。」「如何是超佛越祖？」師云：「提起三十棒。」僧一喝，師拍掌三下。病中，上堂。「維摩病在毘耶城，老僧病在聚雲寺，兩箇無孔鐵鎚，一前一後相似。今日若有人問話，但只搖手。如云：『不會。』向道：『老僧感冒傷風，失了聲氣。』」元旦上堂。舉：「長沙岑遊山歸，首座問：『遊山事作麼生？』岑云：『始從芳草去，又逐落花回。』座云：『大似春意。』岑云：『也勝秋露滴芙蓉。』若有人問聚雲：『遊山事作麼生？』但道：『倒騎鐵馬飛金雨，呀吒獅子吼雲騰。』若問：『長沙和尚語中帶有春意，因甚和尚全無？』但道：『去年正月也有今日，前年正月也有今日，明年正月也有今日，後年正月也有今日，晝夜十二時，九十六成經，三百六十日，二十四成綸，和氣暖風調宇宙，大地何方不是春？』」崇禎丁丑二月望日，尹參府遂江居士請師於巴臺禪院結制。山門。「十方薄伽梵，一路涅槃門。既是一路涅槃門，也不須門外打之遶。」佛殿。「金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，如何即得？」立定，云：「佛陀耶。」展具，云：「達磨耶。」合十，云：「僧伽耶。」禮拜起，復云：「聻。」方丈。「古人喚作方丈地，老僧喚作方丈室。將來烹佛煉祖，道是衲僧巴鼻。」喝一喝。上堂。拈香罷，維那白槌，師隨喝一喝，云：「玄要料揀，賓主照用，一並漏逗了也。若也不會，聽取一偈：野寺孤明夜月斜，高臺飛閣遠人家，綠水金輝浮桂影，青山玉曉墮霜華。」問：「心佛與眾生是三無差別，如何是心？」師云：「門前幾竿竹。」進云：「如何是佛？」師云：「嶺上數株松。」進云：「還有眾生也無？」師云：「心佛與眾生是三無差別。」僧

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 一片，更於何處覓封疆。趙州勘婆子。頌：蕩蕩一條官驛路，行人往往問前津，自從勘破歸來也，誰觸長安車馬塵。趙州因秀才問：「佛不違眾生願，是否？」州云：「是。」曰：「某甲欲覓和尚手中拄杖，得否？」州云：「君子不奪人所好。」曰：「某甲非君子。」曰：「我亦不是佛。」頌：當機一拶玄關轉，走馬循環不暫停，趙老雖然能作主，看來也是假惺惺。趙州無字。頌：一朝被蛇傷，怕見斷井索，總然道個無，爭免狂風作。鎮州蘿蔔。頌：鎮州出大蘿蔔，拈來百味俱足，須知不著薑椒，趙老家風別俗。巖頭作渡次，一日因婆子抱個兒來，乃曰：「呈橈舞棹即不問，且道婆子手中兒甚處得來？」頭便打。婆曰：「婆生七子，六個不遇知音，祇這一個也不消得。」便拋向水中。頌：獨泛悠悠一小舟，滄溟突出巨鰲頭，攔腮一掣翻身去，今古長江水自流。張拙秀才看《千佛名經》，問長沙曰：「百千諸佛，但見其名，未審居何國土，還化物也無？」沙曰：「黃鶴樓崔顥題後，秀才還曾題也未？」曰：「未曾。」沙曰：「得閒題取一篇。」頌：百千諸佛居何土，月印長江徹底清，黃鶴樓題崔顥後。至今吟韻許誰賡？長沙一日游山歸，首座曰：「問和尚甚處去來？」沙曰：「游山來。」座曰：「到甚麼處？」沙云：「始從芳草去，又逐落花回。」座曰：「大似春意。」沙曰：「也勝秋露滴芙蓉。」頌：落花舖徑亂啼鶯，無事野人策杖行，踏遍芳叢歸去也，報君春色勝秋榮。巖頭在鄂渚湖，三文錢買個黑撈波，每日撈蝦捕蜆，且恁麼過時。頌：鄂渚州頭生意足，扁舟獨泛出塵俗，乘風一笛過滄溟，煙樹依依江畔宿。南院問僧：「名甚麼？」曰：「普參。」院曰：「忽遇屎橛時如何？」曰：「不審。」院便打。頌：古佛家風輕漏洩，銀蟾出海對君說。對君說，太饒舌，笑殺雲門屎一橛。溈山問仰山：「如何是西來大意？」仰云：「大好燈籠。」頌：大好燈籠，逼塞虛空，西來大意，門對爐峰。僧問龍牙和尚：「蘇嚕蘇嚕，還有西來意也無？」牙云：「蘇嚕蘿嚕。」頌：腳踏毘盧頂上行，從來不識野狐禪，江山風月由君弄，已落胡笳別調弦。風吹別調露真機，直下全提半似痴，其中消息誰能會，試聽春山啼子規。無位真人。頌：酒色之徒，橫眠倒拖。無位真人攔不住，得歡樂處且歡歌。逢人舉手話淆訛，無位真人好大歌，今日分明通一線，大家依樣畫葫蘆。世尊睹明星悟道。頌：明星忽睹豁雙眼，遍界風光不可藏，鼻直眉橫成現事，笑他特地語郎當。忽睹明星也大奇，驚天動地小兒戲，娘生鼻孔突然現，額下橫分兩道眉。黃龍三關。頌：我手何似佛手，喜怒誰

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 始從芳草去，又逐落花回

Senses.Explanation: I went out among fragrant grasses and returned following falling blossoms. The image makes a Chan return from wandering into a direct report of spring, then becomes a test of what was actually seen. Selected source uses: Yezhu in J33nB284, Chuiwan Zhen in J29nB238, Defeng in J38nB411, Tianyin Yuanxiu in J25nB171. The complete saying is the entry unit. The spring scene is not itself proof of realization.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Ying’an Tanhua. On the Buddha's bathing festival, Ying'an Tanhua spans the Buddha's teaching career with Deer Park at its beginning and the Bati River at its end, then says that all this expenditure of effort only makes others laugh. He puts the flower transmission, Bodhidharma's calming of mind and later lineage divisions under the same challenge, comparing them to digging into the ground to find the sky. Yet calling today's rite 'bathing the Buddha' earns blows, while refusing that name is ungrateful. He raises the exchange about bathing this Buddha but not that one and proposes throwing the ladle at the questioner. The place pair sets the scope of his present criticism; the ritual dilemma keeps it from becoming a simple rejection of gratitude or ceremony.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1370.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Huaihai Yuanzhao. At an address requested for a scripture custodian, Huaihai Yuanzhao quotes the World-Honored One as saying that from Deer Park to the Bati River he never spoke a single word. If someone asks where the whole scripture collection came from, Huaihai would answer: do not question Zeng Shen about Zeng Xi; a filial son avoids his father's personal name. The quoted Buddha voice presents the apparent contradiction between a lifetime of teaching and no word spoken. Huaihai's proposed reply shifts attention from demanding an origin for the books to the propriety of naming. It is a pointed analogy within this address, not historical evidence that no sermons occurred.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1392.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuejian. When Li, the monastic registrar, requests an address for scripture reading, Yuejian begins by saying that teaching and the way cannot be made clear without words. He then revoices the Deer Park-to-Bati pair and the claim that no word was spoken, likening Shakyamuni to someone who pours out an immense lake and tries to gather it with one hand. The present use holds verbal teaching together with its limit; it does not authorize discarding the book which concludes the address.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1384.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jue’an Kexiang. At the commemoration of the Buddha's final release, Jue'an Kexiang portrays Shakyamuni as first making a grand gesture at birth and later being unable to gather it back, so that he claims to have spoken no word between Deer Park and the Bati River. 'Whom could that deceive?' Jue'an asks. Even the decision to stop teaching, the marked chest and the displayed feet become mutterings in sleep. He asks how to cure this deeply rooted illness and answers with red peach blossoms, white plum blossoms and a clear true body. The earlier Buddha is the quoted speaker of the pair; Jue'an's intentionally irreverent account tests dependence on a sacred biography rather than neutrally reporting medical or historical facts.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1410.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tanfang Shouzhong. At the completion of court-sponsored scripture reading, Tanfang Shouzhong revoices the pair and the no-word claim, then raises the obvious objection: where did the thousands of written leaves come from? He answers through the Buddha's difficulty in helping beings attached to pleasures and blinded by doubt. Raising his staff, he announces Gautama's arrival and celebrates teaching that relieves suffering, applying its merit to the emperor. Yet this is still not the highest point: his final staff strike accompanies an old villager beating a drum to honor a river god, unaware of the rulers' power. The pair opens a tension between wordless realization and effective public teaching; it does not erase the actual reading ritual.

He says Gautama foresaw later attachment to its formulations and therefore claimed to have spoken no word from Deer Park to the Bati River. Wu'an continues through collections, commentaries and transmission to argue for seeing one's own mind rather than taking written study as the ultimate attainment. The pair is assigned to Gautama in Wu'an's teaching narrative. Its purported foresight and teaching chronology belong to that argument and should not be mistaken for independently established biography.

Senses.Explanation: Changsha Jingcen goes out following fragrant grass and returns pursuing falling blossoms. He gives the couplet when the head monk asks where his mountain walk led; the follow-up calls it springlike, and Changsha answers that it surpasses autumn dew on the lotus. The Classified Anthology gives Changsha's complete gate-side exchange and preserves several later appraisals warning against treating it merely as poetry. Tianqi Benrui's commentary repeats the exchange, Yuejiang Zhengyin supplies a verse on it, and the nun-master Zukui Fu preserves it before her own verse on leaving and re-entering the grass.

Senses.PreferredTarget: throwing sand and scattering dirt
Senses.Explanation: “Throwing sand and scattering dirt” disparages unnecessary verbal display that clouds rather than clarifies the matter. Yuanwu Keqin contrasts it with a mouth gone unused and a mind like dead wood, then admits that speaking that night is already such activity. Xuedou Chongxian pairs it with raising old sayings and says direct freedom from business is still a featureless iron hammer. Dahui Zonggao places explaining past and present under the same image and contrasts it with hunger, thirst, sitting, and sleep. Poshan Haiming answers a monk’s claim that the present command forbids throwing sand and dirt, turning the charge back into an exchange. Dai’an Puzhuang juxtaposes wielding the sword with throwing sand and asks why both occur together. Guyan Bi places the image among inherited verbal mechanisms that can pin people in place.
Senses.Note: The image is figurative: words and demonstrations can fill the air with grit. Context decides whether the speaker condemns it or deliberately performs it.

Senses.Explanation: To throw a brick to draw out jade is to offer something deliberately lesser in hopes of eliciting something finer. Hanxiu Ruqian and Langting Jingting retell Zhaozhou inviting questions as throwing a brick, only to draw out another clod. Shending Yikui praises an official's attempt to elicit jade but says he still missed his household treasure. Zhufeng Zhenxu applies the image to Shakyamuni eliciting Mahakasyapa, while Tianyin Yuanxiu accepts a layman's letter as a successful brick that reveals his capacity. Chan use therefore tests both halves of the tactic: what bait is offered and whether the response is actually jade.

Senses.Explanation: “Cast the line and throw the hook” is an active fishing image for setting out an encounter, lure, or response. Senses.Note: The line puts a mountain felling gale beside stillness and racing rivers beside nonflow. Feiyin says yesterday has not simply vanished and today has not simply arrived. Senses.Explanation: Autumn wind crosses the Wei River while fallen leaves fill Chang'an: a seasonal scene in which movement at the river and its result in the capital arrive together. Muchen Daomin tests whether this familiar line fits his occasion; Wuzu Fayan answers an opening challenge with it, while Biefeng Yin and Mixing Jiren's questioner use it to close a demand for words beyond words or to expose a misheard answer. Muchen Daomin considers and rejects the line as half a month too early for his beginning-of-autumn address. Biefeng Yin gives it after asking how one meets apart from sound, form, and words. Wuzu Fayan answers an interlocutor challenging him to exercise the ancestral command. An unnamed questioner repeats it to Mixing Jiren, who replies that he has mistaken a bell for a jar.

Senses.Explanation: One instruction says that in traveling on foot and dwelling in the world one must first “establish firm footing, not be stirred by the eight winds” (立定腳跟，不被八風所鼓). A verse places it as a rock amid vast waves; a public exchange receives the direct interjection, “establish firm footing well” (立定腳跟好). The corpus also corrects a rigid use of the phrase: Zhean Jingfan says that always establishing firm footing can, upon close examination, be “a one-sided, withered understanding and a dull fellow who does not comprehend adaptation” (偏枯見解、不達權變之笨漢). Zen therefore bends bodily footing into a recurrent instruction and appraisal for remaining steady, while preserving a recorded warning that immobility itself can be faulted.

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 得成。祖師門下，斷臂立雪，腰石舂碓，擔麥推車
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 法之，轉相勉勵，追復古風，切忌希名苟利，茲深祝也。馬祖昔歸鄉，以簸箕之譏，畏難行道，因再出峽，緣會江西。大隋昔歸鄉，先於龍懷路口，三載茶湯結眾緣，遂隱於木菴，道行於蜀。香林昔歸鄉，潛神隱照於水晶宮，成四十年一片事，撥正智門老祚尋出，雪竇大雲門正宗或留再出，皆以緣斷。今既萬里西歸，但存行脚本志，亦不必拘去留也。慈明昔辭汾陽，祝云：修造自有人，且與佛法為主。自爾五據大剎，不動一椽，唯提振臨際正宗，遂得楊岐、黃龍、翠巖三大士，而子孫徧寰海，果不辜所付授。蓋古人擇可以荷擔之士，不輕如此。信嚴飾壯麗，梵苑未足以奇佛法也。佛道懸曠，久受勤苦，乃可得成。祖師門下，斷臂立雪，腰石舂碓，擔麥推車，事園作飯，開田疇，施湯茶，般土拽磨，皆抗志絕俗，自強不息，圖成功業者乃能之，所謂未有一法從嬾墮懈怠中生。既以洞達淵源，至難至險，人所不能達者尚能，而於涉世應酬，屈節俯仰，而謂不能，此不為非不能也。當稍按下雲頭，自警自䇿，庶幾方便門寬曠，不亦善乎。示裕書記(住杭州靈隱佛智禪師)示裕書記脚蹋實地，到安穩處，時中無虗棄底工夫，綿綿不漏絲毫，湛寂凝然，佛祖莫知，魔外無捉摸，是自住無所住大解脫。雖歷無窮劫，亦只如如地，況復諸緣耶？安住是中，方可建立，與人拔楔抽釘，亦只令渠無住著去，此謂之大事因緣。如來有密語，迦葉不覆藏。迦葉不覆藏，乃如來真密

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 祖大師服勤累年，至於立雪斷臂，而達磨僅以一言
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 一切眾生皆自有之，只為智體無性無依，不能自了，會緣方了。且無明住地煩惱，如何是成諸佛不動智？理極深玄，絕難曉達。雲菴曰：此最分明，易可了解。時有童子方掃除，呼之回首。雲菴指曰：不是不動智。却問：如何是汝佛性？童子左右視，惘然而去。雲庵曰：不是住地煩惱。若能了之，即今成佛。又甞問講師曰：火災起時，山河大地皆被焚盡，世間空虗，是否？對曰：教有明文，安有不是之理？雲庵曰：如許多灰燼，將置何處？講師舌大而乾，笑曰：不知。雲庵亦大笑曰：汝所講者，紙上語耳。其樂說無礙之辨，答則出人意表，問則學者喪氣。盖無師自然之智，非世智可當，真一代法施主也。二祖大師服勤累年，至於立雪斷臂，而達磨僅以一言語之。牛頭懶融，枯禪窮山，初無意於有聞，而四祖自往說法。祖師之於師弟子之際，其必有旨耶？楊文公談苑記沙門寶誌銅牌記讖未來事云：有一真人在冀川，開口張弓在左邊，子子孫孫萬萬年。江南中主名其子曰弘冀，吳越錢鏐諸子皆連弘字，期以應之，而宣祖之諱正當之也。又記周世宗悉毀銅像鑄錢，謂宰相曰：佛教以謂頭目髓腦有利於眾生，尚無所惜，寧復以銅像愛乎？銅州大悲甚靈，應當擊毀。以斧擊其胸，鑱破之。太祖親見其事。後世宗北征，病疽發胸間，咸謂其報應，太祖因信重釋教。歐陽文忠公歸田錄首記太祖初幸相國寺，問僧錄贊寧：可拜佛否？寧奏曰：不拜。問其故，寧曰：見在佛不

Occurrences.Kwic: 儀漢節回，芙蓉花親承雨露。粥足，飯足，三百六十日，合火話家私。僧耶？俗耶？三萬六千場，對床論夢事。垂垂白髮，守先帝、遺墨猶新，視媚草夭花成造化。苟竊世榮，汗顏如雨。丹霞淳禪師丹霞淳禪師師嗣芙蓉，諱子淳，劒州賈氏子。師上堂，舉：德山云：我宗無語句，亦無一法與人。德山恁麼說話，只知入草求人，不覺通身泥水。子細看來，只具一隻眼。丹霞則不然，我宗有語句，金刀剪不開，深深玄妙旨，石女夜懷胎。示眾，舉：肇法師云：乾坤之內，宇宙之間，中有一寶，秘在形山。肇法師恁麼道，只解指蹤話跡，且不能指示於人。丹霞今日劈開宇宙，打破形山，為諸人拈出，具眼者辨取。卓一下。還見麼？鷺󰭇立雪非同色，明月蘆花不似他。上堂：寶月流輝，澄潭有影，水無蘸月之意，月無分照之心，水月兩忘，方可稱斷。所以道：昇天底事直須颺却，十成底事直須去却，擲地金聲不須回顧。若能如是，始解異類中行。諸人到者裏還相委悉麼？良久，云：當行不舉人間步，披毛戴角混泥塵。上堂：亭亭日午猶虧半，寂寂三更尚未圓，六戶不曾知曉意，往來常在月明前。僧問：牛頭未見四祖時如何？曰：金菊乍開蜂競採。曰：見後如何？曰：苗枯花謝了無依。真歇參次，師問：如何是空劫已前自己？歇擬對，師曰：儞閙在，且去。一日，登鉢盂峯，忽悟，歸侍立。師掌曰：將謂儞知有歇。忻然拜之。翌日，上堂：日照孤峯翠，月臨溪水寒。

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 卓一下。還見麼？鷺󰭇立雪非同色，明月蘆花不似
ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 儀漢節回，芙蓉花親承雨露。粥足，飯足，三百六十日，合火話家私。僧耶？俗耶？三萬六千場，對床論夢事。垂垂白髮，守先帝、遺墨猶新，視媚草夭花成造化。苟竊世榮，汗顏如雨。丹霞淳禪師丹霞淳禪師師嗣芙蓉，諱子淳，劒州賈氏子。師上堂，舉：德山云：我宗無語句，亦無一法與人。德山恁麼說話，只知入草求人，不覺通身泥水。子細看來，只具一隻眼。丹霞則不然，我宗有語句，金刀剪不開，深深玄妙旨，石女夜懷胎。示眾，舉：肇法師云：乾坤之內，宇宙之間，中有一寶，秘在形山。肇法師恁麼道，只解指蹤話跡，且不能指示於人。丹霞今日劈開宇宙，打破形山，為諸人拈出，具眼者辨取。卓一下。還見麼？鷺󰭇立雪非同色，明月蘆花不似他。上堂：寶月流輝，澄潭有影，水無蘸月之意，月無分照之心，水月兩忘，方可稱斷。所以道：昇天底事直須颺却，十成底事直須去却，擲地金聲不須回顧。若能如是，始解異類中行。諸人到者裏還相委悉麼？良久，云：當行不舉人間步，披毛戴角混泥塵。上堂：亭亭日午猶虧半，寂寂三更尚未圓，六戶不曾知曉意，往來常在月明前。僧問：牛頭未見四祖時如何？曰：金菊乍開蜂競採。曰：見後如何？曰：苗枯花謝了無依。真歇參次，師問：如何是空劫已前自己？歇擬對，師曰：儞閙在，且去。一日，登鉢盂峯，忽悟，歸侍立。師掌曰：將謂儞知有歇。忻然拜之。翌日，上堂：日照孤峯翠，月臨溪水寒。

Senses.PreferredTarget: request instruction
Senses.Explanation: To request instruction is to approach an instructor for an answer, clarification, or further examination. The Blue Cliff Record uses the term as a named question-type and distinguishes a long-standing student's request after seeing but not penetrating or penetrating but not clarifying. Other records use it for a first announced request, an attendant's follow-up after an exchange, and biographical visits to an instructor. These are uses of the same act of asking to receive further explanation; noun and verb grammar do not make separate senses.
Senses.Note: Across the collected corpus the expression has 1,949 exact occurrences in 310 distinct works. Eight anchors cover direct requests, narrated teacher-student visits, follow-up questioning, and explicit classification of the request-for-instruction question across distinct works.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Śākyamuni
Senses.Explanation: Śākyamuni, the name by which the Chan corpus identifies the buddha of its founding cases. The Ancestral Hall Collection gives the in-corpus name gloss: “Śākyamuni: translated, it says ‘Able and Benevolent’” (釋迦者，譯言能仁也). The record then bends the name through case and appraisal. It names Śākyamuni as the one who holds up the flower before Kāśyapa’s smile and as the one who mounts the seat before Mañjuśrī strikes the sounding block. It also makes him the subject of public questions: Yunmen answers “What is Śākyamuni’s body?” (如何是釋迦身) with “a dry shit-stick” (乾屎橛). Other recorded appraisals are equally direct: Guoqing Feng calls Śākyamuni “an ox-headed jailer” (牛頭獄卒), and Shaoshan describes him as “the general of a defeated army” (敗軍之將), alongside Kāśyapa as “a man who has lost his life” (喪身失命底人). Nantái Yungong says, “Śākyamuni has already perished; Maitreya has not yet been born” (釋迦已滅，彌勒未生), then raises the whisk and locates the handling of the buddha-teaching in that day’s teaching seat. The deviation is this range: the proper name is not protected as a remote sacred biography; it is a recurrent actor in the flower and seat cases, a subject put into public questions, and a figure whom masters openly compare, re-stage, and appraise.
Senses.Note: The 6,608 exact matches occur in 395 allowlisted files. “Śākyamuni” is the name-form. “The World-Honored One” is a title used heavily in the flower, seat, and silence cases; “old man Śākyamuni” is a longer familiar form with its own strongly marked Chan deployment. Matches inside the longer form overlap mechanically but do not erase that lexical distinction.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Shakyamuni never appeared in the world; Bodhidharma never came from the west
SearchAliases: shakyamuni never appeared in the world; bodhidharma never came from the west
Senses.Note: The saying imagines that Shakyamuni never appeared and Bodhidharma never arrived. Chaozong says the matter is present before and after either founder, then points to night, day, hunger, and thirst. Miyin says leaves, birds, streams, and wind continue to speak. Yushan calls the imagined earlier time peaceful, then asks how an assembly would respond if Mount Sumeru entered their nostrils. Liaoan uses the line when closing a retreat and notes that coming and going do not bind the matter. Chushi gives it to a monk, followed by ordinary bodies and seasons. The counterfactual tests whether listeners rely on an inherited event to see what is at hand.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Shakyamuni is gone, and Maitreya has yet to be born
AlternateTargets: The Buddha of the past has passed away; the future Buddha is not yet born
SearchAliases: Shakyamuni gone Maitreya not yet born
Senses.Note: “Shakyamuni has passed away; Maitreya has not yet been born” opens a gap and asks who carries the teaching now. Baichi asks whose hand holds the staff at a temple entrance; Liao’an asks on the Buddha’s birthday what is being bathed; Xiaoyin puts the lineage’s life in the hand of his current assembly; Duanqiao makes his staff speak in the interval; Xueyan asks who can proclaim and carry out the teaching across the intervening years. The pair names a present responsibility between two figures, rather than merely dating an era.

Entries.SourceTerm: 釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來

Senses.PreferredTarget: Shakyamuni has passed; Maitreya has yet to come
AlternateTargets: The Buddha Shakyamuni is gone and Maitreya is still to arrive
SearchAliases: Shakyamuni gone Maitreya not yet arrived
between Shakyamuni and Maitreya present Chan
Senses.Note: Miyun and Feiyin speak this pair at Buddha halls and ask who holds the teaching in the interval; Chaozong uses it to answer a question about receiving a prediction of Buddhahood; Jiqi says the eye of the teaching has been entrusted to the present; and Xingkong names the open ground between past and future. The historical Buddhas are the subjects of the line, while each named current master is its speaker in the selected source. A related public Nanquan saying denies a fixed place for Maitreya; this pair instead makes the interval between past and future Buddhas a present responsibility.

Occurrences.Kwic: 李翱太守嚮藥山玄化，屢請不赴，一日躬謁，因藥山看經執卷不顧，侍者云：『太守在此。』守褊性急云：『見面不如聞名。』拂袖而出，藥山曰：『太守何得貴耳賤目？』守回拱謝，問曰：『如何是道？』藥山以手指上下曰：『會麼？』守曰：『不會。』藥山曰：『雲在青天水在瓶。』守欣愜作禮而述偈曰：『鍊得身形似鶴形，千株松下兩函經，我來問道無餘說，雲在青天水在瓶。』據李翱問得甚妙，藥山答得更奇，一主一賓激揚個事，千百年後猶令人啟發悟由，可謂法門一時盛事。秪如今日太尊忽若問山僧：『如何是道？』即答云：『日坐公堂應萬機，分明都是自家底。』且道與古人答處親疏相去多少？試分析看。」遂喝一喝，卓拄杖下座。順治六年九月初八日，松江府紳衿王元瑞、曹勳、莊元禎、張安茂、單恂、周茂源、陳麟等請住超果寺開堂，於十月二十七日入院，至山門云：「玄文玉作笥，真境妙為門，老僧從此入，衣裓，盛天香。正當入門，為人一句作麼生道？彈指不勞頻斂念，重重樓閣應時開。」喝一喝便入。佛殿，云：「釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來，現在法柄在阿誰手裏？三泖水沿門，九峰霞照寺，頻唱無生曲，是人增意氣。如何是無生曲？」以坐具作拈笛勢，遂禮拜。伽藍堂，云：「降魔杵、摧邪劍，憑君拈弄，演法脈、闡宗風，還我主持。海眾雲集，慧命在斯，仰賴神護，望勿差池。」祖師堂，云：「西歸一隻履，大地人挂齒，始祖大宗師，去得不乾淨，帶累二三，單傳五宗，並峙今日，敬燒一把清香，平空要與出氣。」方丈，云：「辨龍蛇句，明縱奪機，坐此室、行此令，正是其時，凡是英靈衲子，頂門都與一錐。」遂喝一喝，據坐。當日眾請上堂，師至座前拈請啟云：「弘揚正法眼藏，贊弼教外別傳，須是諸鄉紳大護法始得，恐大眾欲聞、仰煩書記對眾宣讀。」宣疏畢，師指法座云：「毘盧高座，人人有志上頭行，山僧今日又向人天眾前潑水撒沙去也。」遂陞拈香云：「者一瓣香，洪蒙未判之先，陰陽未動之際，爇向爐中，端為祝延今上皇帝萬歲！萬歲！萬萬歲！者一瓣香，齊兩儀、合四象，爇向爐中，奉為滿朝文武天下官僚普同供養。者一瓣香，積代簪纓、奕世金玉，爇向爐中，奉為合府鄉紳、本山護法，伏願屏翰禪林多意氣，匡扶祖道永聯芳。者一瓣香，恩深無語、懷抱分明，次第六回拈出，爇向爐中，專為傳曹溪正脈三十四世中興天童本師密雲悟老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。」遂斂衣就座。上

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 李翱太守嚮藥山玄化，屢請不赴，一日躬謁，因藥山看經執卷不顧，侍者云：『太守在此。』守褊性急云：『見面不如聞名。』拂袖而出，藥山曰：『太守何得貴耳賤目？』守回拱謝，問曰：『如何是道？』藥山以手指上下曰：『會麼？』守曰：『不會。』藥山曰：『雲在青天水在瓶。』守欣愜作禮而述偈曰：『鍊得身形似鶴形，千株松下兩函經，我來問道無餘說，雲在青天水在瓶。』據李翱問得甚妙，藥山答得更奇，一主一賓激揚個事，千百年後猶令人啟發悟由，可謂法門一時盛事。秪如今日太尊忽若問山僧：『如何是道？』即答云：『日坐公堂應萬機，分明都是自家底。』且道與古人答處親疏相去多少？試分析看。」遂喝一喝，卓拄杖下座。順治六年九月初八日，松江府紳衿王元瑞、曹勳、莊元禎、張安茂、單恂、周茂源、陳麟等請住超果寺開堂，於十月二十七日入院，至山門云：「玄文玉作笥，真境妙為門，老僧從此入，衣裓，盛天香。正當入門，為人一句作麼生道？彈指不勞頻斂念，重重樓閣應時開。」喝一喝便入。佛殿，云：「釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來，現在法柄在阿誰手裏？三泖水沿門，九峰霞照寺，頻唱無生曲，是人增意氣。如何是無生曲？」以坐具作拈笛勢，遂禮拜。伽藍堂，云：「降魔杵、摧邪劍，憑君拈弄，演法脈、闡宗風，還我主持。海眾雲集，慧命在斯，仰賴神護，望勿差池。」祖師堂，云：「西歸一隻履，大地人挂齒，始祖大宗師，去得不乾淨，帶累二三，單傳五宗，並峙今日，敬燒一把清香，平空要與出氣。」方丈，云：「辨龍蛇句，明縱奪機，坐此室、行此令，正是其時，凡是英靈衲子，頂門都與一錐。」遂喝一喝，據坐。當日眾請上堂，師至座前拈請啟云：「弘揚正法眼藏，贊弼教外別傳，須是諸鄉紳大護法始得，恐大眾欲聞、仰煩書記對眾宣讀。」宣疏畢，師指法座云：「毘盧高座，人人有志上頭行，山僧今日又向人天眾前潑水撒沙去也。」遂陞拈香云：「者一瓣香，洪蒙未判之先，陰陽未動之際，爇向爐中，端為祝延今上皇帝萬歲！萬歲！萬萬歲！者一瓣香，齊兩儀、合四象，爇向爐中，奉為滿朝文武天下官僚普同供養。者一瓣香，積代簪纓、奕世金玉，爇向爐中，奉為合府鄉紳、本山護法，伏願屏翰禪林多意氣，匡扶祖道永聯芳。者一瓣香，恩深無語、懷抱分明，次第六回拈出，爇向爐中，專為傳曹溪正脈三十四世中興天童本師密雲悟老和尚，用酬法乳之恩。」遂斂衣就座。上

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 果然吞得跳得，經依舊是經，棒依舊是棒，經還釋迦老子，棒還黃檗大師，於諸人分上總淺交涉。然雖如是，只如興化於大覺脫下衲衣，痛與一頓，言下悟得臨濟先師在黃檗處喫棒底道理又作麼生？玅觸宣明佛子住，遺身純覺拂蒿枝。」下座。上堂。師舉諸佛出身處話，云：「東山行水上，雲門坐斷千差；薰風自南來，佛果尋常一味。高峰道：『二老雖具頂門正眼，愨其本源，天地懸隔。』雖然，高峰也是填墨順朱，未解證龜成鱉。須知壁立萬仞處淨裸裸，平田淺艸裏峭危危，十字街頭相逢卻在千峰頂上握手，千峰頂上相逢卻在十字街頭握手，便見二老主賓互換、著著出身之機。既然如是，只如永明壽禪師道：『石牛生象子，木女孕嬰兒，諸佛從中出，最初成道時。』意作麼生？不許夜行，投明須到。」復舉：「僧禮拜天童密雲和尚次，童云：『拜作甚麼？』僧云：『求授記作佛。』童云：『直饒作得，也是分外。』」師云：「先師雖是一期剿絕，未免語上偏枯，令者僧至今坐在萬仞峰頭轉身不得。今日寶華有求授記作佛者，但向他道：『釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來。』管教他如龍得水、似虎靠山。」下座。四月八日，檀越供法衣，請上堂。師云：「佛佛授手，咸此法衣。彌勒千丈之軀，披來不短；釋迦丈六之身，搭來不長。今日披在寶華身上，耀古騰今，光明赫奕，正偏咸稱，左右逢源，入淨入穢，現土現身，利物應機，辨魔簡異。臨濟道：『我共你入淨玅國土中，著清淨衣說法身佛；入無差別國土中，著無差別衣說報身佛；入解脫國土中，著光明衣說化身佛。』三種國土皆是依變。諸人當知：一切佛法，教則頓漸偏圓、宗則三玄五位，皆是衣，不得在衣上認青、認黃、認赤、認白，須認著衣底人方有入作分。彩雲影裏仙人現，手把紅羅扇遮面，急須著眼看仙人，莫看仙人手中扇。寶華今日將佛衣、法衣一時脫卻，應時即事為諸人露箇消息去也。」良久，云：「𩖼𩖼熏風來入奏，赤條條地我為尊。」下座。慧雲禪人請上堂。師云：「大事未明，如喪考妣，無明貪愛本無依，廢寢忘食成分外。大事已明，如喪考妣，智度方便閒家具，泥牛入海杳無蹤。今日慧雲上座請寶華陞座說法以薦考妣，且道所薦底考妣是無明貪愛邪？智度方便邪？」良久，云：「當陽薦取自家底，下載清風付與誰？」下座。上堂。云：「若論此事，忒煞現成。佛祖未出世以前也恁麼，佛祖既出世以後也恁麼，即今以至盡未來際也恁麼，亙古亙今，騎聲

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 諸方樣子施行。設法不嚴，道化日見凌替，罪歸阿誰？未若眾中得一人出來，真贗虛實向這裡定當得下。活活底虛空，搖杌不動，何患天下不太平？」一僧巍巍堂堂而出，師曰：「不是你。」便落座。先皇帝諱日，上堂。拈香已，就座。良久，乃起立曰：「年年此日，不得忘卻。」下座。上堂。舉：「鼓山和尚因僧問：『如何是西來意？』山曰：『石人筆下看。』」師曰：「大哉！從上之心髓。又問：『如何是作家？』山曰：『你行腳為什麼？』」師曰：「亦不是戲論。僧曰：『與麼即某甲不疑也。』山曰：『你何處得作家？』」師曰：「亦不是亂塞人口。」良久，長聲歎曰：「追遠之誠，何可忘也？」隨顧一眾曰：「汝等從前所作殺、盜、婬、妄諸罪，一一如湯消冰，應念化成無上知覺。苟或毫末不靈，秪因聽響各流傳，又從今日起。」跳下座，旋風趁散。住蘇州靈嵒崇報寺語一住蘇州靈嵒崇報寺語到寺上堂。「靈源獨耀，千日蔽其光輝；一岳盤空，萬象失其相好。大丈夫！秉慧劍，般若鋒兮金剛燄，非但空摧外道心，早曾落卻天魔膽。釋迦已過去，彌勒猶未來，如來正法眼藏委在今日，捏聚放開總繇這裏。放開也，無量諸佛國土一時現前，且聽諸人飽足觀光；捏聚也，天下老和尚鼻孔一串穿卻，又向什麼處出氣？」喝一喝，曰：「巍巍乎！惟天為大，惟堯則之；蕩蕩乎！民無能名焉。」卓拄杖，下座。上堂。僧問：「上來納個不審作家禪客，下去賞個珍重本分宗師。秪如雲興百問、缾瀉千酬底，當得何名？」師不畣，僧曰：「欲得不辜來意，更請別轉一機。」師亦不畣，僧曰：「某甲也是譬如閒。」師哂之，乃曰：「三世諸佛說夢，有事有理；六代祖師說夢，無黨無偏。靈嵒今日說夢，黃連未是苦，黃柏可為憐。何故？近來世界大非昔比，行腳高士朝也妄想、暮也妄想，收得安南又憂塞北，那討閒心情來聽說夢？縱饒勉強築在他耳竅裏，生門易過、死門難出，今日也恁麼、明日也恁麼。雪竇道得好：『第三、第四不問你，後五日事作麼生？』說到這裡，未免二乘膽戰、十地魂驚，老漢更不與你方便，直待驢年諾惺惺著，吾行爾隨、吾喚爾應，一隨一應，無少無剩。」上堂。舉：「趙州和尚示眾曰：『金佛不度爐，木佛不度火，泥佛不度水，真佛屋裏坐。』」師曰：「至道無難，惟嫌揀擇。選佛場開，是聖是凡一齊來。心空及第，所作所為絕猜忌。不見石頭土塊，草木叢林，以至昧略飛搖，我皆令入無餘涅槃而滅度之

Senses.Explanation: 'Shakyamuni and Maitreya' names the present and future buddhas together. Chan masters repeatedly place the pair below an unnamed 'other': Nanyan calls them his servants, Yuanwu says they dare not take the lead, and Muchen Daomin repeats the servant formula before sending the assembly to tea. Nanyan Sheng says that however immeasurably great Shakyamuni and Maitreya are, they remain his servants. Yuanwu Keqin says that even Shakyamuni and Maitreya dare not set their eyes at the head of his proclamation. Muchen Daomin raises Wuzu Fayan's servant question, faults Wuzu for keeping the fruit to himself, and restates it for the assembly.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。「廣額屠兒放下屠刀云：『我是千佛一數。』平地登高易。文殊師利乃七佛之師，於迦文會裏作弟子。從空放下難。不落因果，五百生墮野狐身，為甚麼卻作人語？不昧因果，當下脫野狐身，猶有野狐氣息。在眾中還有知得龍池落處者麼？苟或知得，不妨出來剖露看。如其未然，不見道？釋迦彌勒是他奴，那箇男兒不丈夫？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB182.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanru. Wanru Tongwei recounts a butcher putting down his knife and claiming, ‘I am one of the thousand buddhas,’ then calls climbing from level ground easy. He contrasts Manjushri, teacher of seven buddhas, appearing as a disciple in Shakyamuni’s assembly: coming down from the sky is hard. He next puts the fox account’s ‘not falling into cause and effect’ beside ‘not obscuring cause and effect.’ He asks whether anyone knows where Longchi stands and can show it, then says, ‘Shakyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves; what man is not a man of mettle?’ The concluding challenge follows these reversals of elevated and low standing, not a report about actual slave ownership.

Occurrences.Kwic: 出門步步清猋起，一棹鐵船三萬里，大魚剛被小魚吞，縮却龍頭展虵尾。未到中原俱歷徧，浙山如黛江如練，臨風側耳聽鄉談，故國依然海西岸。佛不論先後，道不揀精麤，禪不屬迷悟，智不得有無。釋迦彌勒是他奴，那箇男兒不丈夫？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi. Chushi Fanqi’s farewell poem for Cong describes traveling out from home, rivers and hills, hearing the old country’s speech, and a homeland across the sea. Its final lines say, ‘Buddha is not judged by earlier and later; the Way does not pick refinement or roughness. Chan does not belong to confusion and awakening; discernment does not fall under having and not having. Shakyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves; what man is not a man of mettle?’ The ending addresses Cong in a farewell that has just refused several ways of ranking or fixing the matter.

Senses.Explanation: A forceful challenge puts Shakyamuni and Maitreya in a subordinate position and asks who is not a man of mettle. The wording addresses the hearer’s standing through the language of slaves and capable men. Wanru Tongwei prepares the challenge through contrary changes of standing. A butcher sets down his knife and claims a place among a thousand buddhas; Manjushri, teacher of seven buddhas, appears as a disciple. Wanru then raises the two cause-and-effect replies from the fox account and asks who can show where Longchi stands. ‘Shakyamuni and Maitreya are his slaves’ belongs to this escalating challenge, followed by the question whether any man is not a man of mettle. The words supply no separately named owner for ‘his.’ Chushi Fanqi ends a farewell poem for Cong with the same pair. After images of travel and hearing the home country’s speech, he refuses earlier/later for buddhas, refined/rough for the Way, confusion/awakening for Chan, and having/not having for discernment. The closing claim then places the two named buddhas below the figure addressed by the couplet and challenges the departing man’s standing. This is the poem’s rhetorical ordering, not a biographical statement that either buddha was someone’s slave.

Senses.Explanation: Shakyamuni and Maitreya are still his servants is the declaration that opens a recurring testing question: who is he? The records preserve the pronoun rather than resolving it into a doctrinal name. In Dahui Zonggao's discourse, a monk asks about both the saying attributed to Nanquan and Wuzu Fayan's public raising; Dahui answers that claimed recognition already falls into ranking and that he has already answered. Hongjue Min quotes Wuzu's version, faults it for knowing self but not others, and then gives his own version before calling the assembly to tea. Changson uses the formula directly to test a monk and supplies 'there is no tail behind' only after the monk cannot answer. Dangui says that this 'he' is not absent and that Shakyamuni and Maitreya recognize him because they have served him, but still asks who he is. The phrase therefore lowers the named buddhas beneath an unnamed referent while making any proposed identification part of the encounter's test.

Senses.PreferredTarget: old man Śākyamuni
Senses.Explanation: Old man Śākyamuni: a familiar name-form that repeatedly removes ceremonial distance in the Chan record. Longji Shaoxiu raises his staff and cries, “Old man Śākyamuni has arrived!” (釋迦老子來也) as his answer to “What is great function appearing?” (如何是大用現前). Dahui Zonggao likewise raises the whisk and says that the old man has arrived, then asks whether the assembly sees him. Shoushan Xingnian says that even if old man Śākyamuni came there, he would receive thirty blows; Dahui comments on a story of Śākyamuni disputing the buddha-teaching with Indra by saying, “This old fellow deserves thirty staff-blows” (這老漢好與三十拄杖). The form also remains a quotation label: Yunmen Wenyan says, “Old man Śākyamuni has already spoken; Maitreya still does not know” (釋迦老子道了也彌勒猶自不知). Shanhui says, “Speak a sentence where old man Śākyamuni could not speak; take a step where the great teacher Bodhidharma could not go” (釋迦老子說不到處，說取一句；達磨大師行不到處，行取一步). Yuanwu Keqin quotes old man Śākyamuni’s saying about one person truly returning to the source, contrasts Wuzu Fayan’s version, and then supplies his own wording. The strongest coarse appraisal is textual and explicit: Deshan Xuanjian says, “Śākyamuni is a dry shit-stick” (釋迦老子是乾屎橛), paired with “Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are shit-carrying fellows” (文殊普賢是擔屎漢). The deviation lies in the form’s repeated Chan use: a revered name becomes an immediately addressable “old man” whom named masters quote, enact, out-say, rebuke, and strike in public discourse.
Senses.Note: The exact longer form occurs 2,409 times in 281 allowlisted files. The suffix “old man” (老子) is translated rather than omitted: it is what distinguishes this headword from bare “Śākyamuni” (釋迦). The examples preserve separate deployment classes—quotation label, enacted arrival, comparison, rebuke, and coarse appraisal—rather than treating every overlap with the shorter name as equivalent.

Senses.Explanation: The five graphs are the fixed first leg of the formula that leaves each named one on his own side: Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni — his affair, not yours. Dahui Zonggao closes his sermon for the Qian household on the Angulimala story with it: if you see into the point where the new-comer's skill and the awakened one's power both fail, then the old Shakyamuni is Angulimala and Angulimala is the old Shakyamuni; if not, Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni and Angulimala is Angulimala — no business of the household in labor. Yuanwu Keqin spent it twice: his informal talk sets it in a fourfold row — Shakyamuni, Maitreya, freedom, Sudhana each on his own — for the one whose mind-machinery has broken through and who kicks up and walks the moment it is raised; and his Blue Cliff Record commentary on the medicine-and-sickness case sets Deshan's staff and Linji's shout aside — let that be — Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Maitreya is Maitreya — before warning that those who do not know the landing place read it as medicine matched to sickness. Xutang Zhiyu, on the day of the nirvana, pairs Shakyamuni with Mara himself: the great awakened one showed the form of passing into stillness amid the hundred flowers in full glory; monks who can set one eye on this — Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Mara is Mara. Liao'an Qingyu answers the birth question with it: before the Buddha came into the world — Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni; after — Maitreya is Maitreya; and whose prediction does he receive, since he received none from Dipankara? — each one draws his own belly. Xiatang Huiyuan seals his letter to the retired vice-minister with it: hold firm, be your own master, sit astride right and wrong — Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Maitreya is Maitreya; what do they hinder in me? Yanxi Guangwen opens his Wanshou temple's Buddha hall with it — one sitting-mat of ground, whose is it not? — and the lamp of 1101 transmits Raozhou Jianfu Daoying's address ending: if you can be thus, you will see Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni and the First Patriarch is the First Patriarch — what bowl of mine has it to do with? Dahui Zonggao's requested sermon for the Qian household works the Angulimala story whole: the thousand-finger crown, the mother's finger, the staff's ring, the household in labor, and his late teacher Zhantang's gloss on it — the gold-dung teaching: not understood it is gold, understood it is dung. The close sets the exchange the formula belongs to: with the great way clear, raise one hair-tip and all is met at once, just like the Angulimala affair — the new-comer's I-am-new-at-this and the awakened one's power both fail, so why was the son born? See into this and the old Shakyamuni is Angulimala; if not, Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni and Angulimala is Angulimala, no business of the household in labor — then the closing dedication for the wife of councilor Qian. His own recorded sayings carry the same sermon. Yuanwu Keqin's two spendings frame the formula's test. The informal talk: essence and function, the thousand devices and the one way before the eyes, all set down — how does one land there? For the one whose mind-machinery has broken through, whose gains and losses are forgotten, who has sent the mysterious away — hearing it raised, he kicks up and walks: Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Maitreya is Maitreya, freedom is freedom, Sudhana is Sudhana. The Blue Cliff Record's case 87, Yunmen's the whole earth is medicine, which is your own self: after the case is stated and Deshan's staff and Linji's shout are set aside, the formula marks the place where the commentators' medicine-matched-to-sickness reading does not reach — the World-honored One's forty-nine years and three hundred assemblies were all medicine given for sickness, honey traded for bitter gourd, and the formula keeps the self from being swallowed by the cure. The later masters kept it as their own coin. Xutang Zhiyu's nirvana-day address: the great awakened one, seeing beings take the false as their ground, showed the form of passing while the hundred flowers shone — monks, if you can set one eye on this, Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni and Mara is Mara. Liao'an Qingyu's exchange at his Benjue temple: before the Buddha came into the world — Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni; after — Maitreya is Maitreya; and pressed on the prediction he did not receive from Dipankara: each one draws his own belly; then his talk on the one who poured a ladle of filthy water on the sages an age of dust ago and, once awakened, is poured on by everyone. Xiatang Huiyuan's answer to the retired vice-minister's parting question — work not reaching, the circle is not round; words not connecting, not kin — glosses the effort-less working of the way, then: hold firm, be your own master, sit astride right and wrong; Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Maitreya is Maitreya — what do they hinder in me? straight through crown to sole, bone to marrow, leaning on nothing. The verse and lamp recensions carry the same verdict in other frames. Yanxi Guangwen's Wanshou record opens with the Buddha hall: one sitting-mat of ground — whose is it not? Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni, Maitreya is Maitreya; does the assembly yet hear the full letting-out and full gathering-in? — then points at the seat: turning downward, who does not know it; turning upward, like ten suns shining at once. The lamp of 1101 transmits Raozhou Jianfu Daoying's hall address — the nameless one with no place, no name, no face; seek him in a thought as small as a dust-mote and ten lifetimes open between; long let him go free, wanting to rise he rises, wanting to stay he stays — no love of life, no fear of death, no seeking of the buddha, no dread of the demon, joining neither the awake nor the troubled, accepting no thing, slighting no thing — if you can be thus, you will see Shakyamuni is Shakyamuni and the First Patriarch is the First Patriarch: what bowl of mine has it to do with? And he closes the address by pricing such talk itself: under the patch-robe gate's cross-examination it still splashes some mud on cloth skirt and straw sandal — how much the more you all everywhere.
